hero.pill: For every family, however it's organised
hero.title: Sorted together. One flow.
hero.lead: Calendar, costs, messages and everything about your children in one place. So you and the other parent know what's happening, and no one has to ask around any more.
hero.note: Free to use · on your phone and your computer

audience.title: Every family works differently. eezzyflow works with yours.
audience.busyBody: Two diaries, school, hobbies and work. See together what's coming up, without endless messages back and forth.
audience.apartBody: Co-parents who live apart: an overview of who the children are with, what still needs doing and what's been paid.
audience.newBody: Set down the schedule, the costs and what your child needs once, without having to talk it through again every time.
audience.soloBody: eezzyflow works on your own too. Appointments, spending and everything about your children together, in one place.

faq.title: Good to know
faq.q1: Does the other parent have to use eezzyflow too?
faq.a1: No. You can start perfectly well on your own. Invite the other parent when it suits you both.
faq.a2: The basics are free: calendar, messages and the costs that concern you. If you want more, you can take Plus or Family later. While the app is in its test phase, everything is open.
faq.q3: What does the other parent see?
faq.a3: Only what concerns your shared children: the calendar, your messages and the costs you share. They don't see your own calendar that you link.
faq.q4: Does it work if we live apart?
faq.a4: Yes, that's what it's made for. You set down the parenting schedule once and eezzyflow fills in the calendar automatically.

cta.title: Less organising. More family.
cta.body: Start for free and invite the other parent when you're ready.
cta.note: Works in your browser, on phone and computer

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Does my ex have to pay too?
faq.a1: No. Each of you chooses. If you pay for Plus, the other parent simply has the free basics, and the other way round.
faq.q2: What if the other parent doesn't want to take part?
faq.a2: Then you use the app on your own. The calendar and costs work for you, and you can always invite them later.
faq.q3: Can we take out one subscription together?
faq.a3: Yes, with Family. Whether you live together or not: one subscription, and you both get everything. One of you pays; add the subscription as a cost in the app and it ends up in your balance, just like your other costs.
faq.a4: Via Settings → Account. You keep access until the end of your billing period.
faq.q5: Can the other parent use my Plus too?
faq.a5: No. What you share, such as the calendar, the children and the costs, you both see. The extra features only work for whoever has Plus or Family themselves.

who.apartBody: Then each of you chooses: whoever takes Plus only pays for themselves, and whoever doesn't pay keeps the free basics. If you both want everything, one Family subscription costs less than Plus twice.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: eezzyflow is about your child. That is why we keep as little data as possible, store it in Europe, and make sure no one outside your family can access it.
privacy.contact: Ask questions about your data through <link>the contact form</link>. You don't need an account for that.

items.1: Your email address, your name and, if you like, a profile photo.
items.2: What you enter about your children: first name, date of birth, photo, parenting schedule, appointments, costs with receipts, documents and messages.
items.3: Health data, only if you enter it yourself under Health (for example allergies, vaccinations or the GP). This is sensitive data: only parents with parental authority see it, and a viewer only sees the allergies.
items.4: Your location, only if you share it yourself at a handover. The other parent sees it for two hours; you can always stop sharing earlier, and the location is then erased.
items.5: The link to your own calendar, if you connect it. We only keep appointments with your child's name or that you approve; we read the rest and forget it straight away.
items.6: Who forms a household together, and the devices on which you want to receive notifications.
items.7: A history of who changed what and when, so you can look back later.

paras2.1: We deliberately don't ask for a national register number or your child's address. If a judgment you have read contains a national register number, the app does not copy it.

paras.1: To make the app work: signing you in, showing your data to the people who have access to it, and letting you see what changed when. The legal basis is the agreement you enter into with us when you create an account.
paras.2: You only enter health data or share your location if you want to. You can always remove them again.

paras.1: Only you and the people you invite. The protection is in the database itself, not just on screen: a parent technically cannot request data from a family they have no role in.

items.1: Your child's other parent sees what you share: the calendar, appointments, the costs that concern them and your messages.
items.2: A viewer (for example grandma or the babysitter) only sees the calendar, important dates, school, GP and allergies. A viewer cannot change anything.
items.3: Your child, with their own account, only sees where they are, their own appointments and photos.
items.4: Your partner in a blended family only sees your children's first names and whether they are home.

paras2.1: We don't sell anything, don't use your data for advertising and don't set trackers or advertising cookies.

paras.1: Everything we keep is stored in the European Union. We work with:

paras2.1: Anthropic only sees something when you yourself press the button to have a judgment, receipt, photo of a school calendar or message read or rewritten. We only keep the answer once you save it. Anthropic does not use that data to train its models.

paras.1: As long as you have an account. If you delete your account, your data is erased. If you share a child with a co-parent, that child remains with that parent: it is their data too.
paras.2: The history keeps the fact that an account was deleted, without your data.
paras.3: We clean up technical traces automatically, every night:

items.1: Sign-in attempts (to prevent abuse): after 24 hours.
items.2: Invitations that were not accepted: 90 days after they expired.
items.3: Ticked-off shopping items: 30 days after ticking them off.
items.4: Suggestions from your own calendar you did nothing with: 30 days after the date.
items.5: Accounts that were never confirmed: after 30 days.
items.6: What you send us through the contact form: after two years.

paras.1: You may access, correct, erase and take your data with you. You download all your data yourself in Settings › Account, where you can also delete your account. For anything else, a message through the contact form is enough.
paras.2: If you disagree with how we handle your data, you can file a complaint with the Belgian Data Protection Authority (dataprotectionauthority.be).

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using eezzyflow, you agree to these terms.

what.title: What eezzyflow is
what.body: An app for parents to arrange where their children stay, share costs and communicate, whether you live apart or together. You use the app at your own responsibility.

who.title: Who may use the app
who.body: Anyone aged 18 or over. A child can get their own, limited account if all parents with parental authority agree.

use.title: What you may do with it
use.body: Use the app for what it is meant for: organising your family life. You may not use it to harass others, spread false information or disrupt how it works.

data.title: Your data
data.body: You keep all rights to what you enter. We only process that data so the app can work. We don't sell anything and use nothing for advertising. See the <link>privacy policy</link> for details.

ai.title: Reading with Claude
ai.body: If you have a judgment, receipt, photo or message read or rewritten, the result is a suggestion. Check it before you save or send it: the app can make mistakes.

payments.title: Payments
payments.body: The basic version is free. For extra features we charge a subscription. Prices are shown in the app. A subscription runs until you cancel it; you can cancel at any time.

liability.title: Liability
liability.body: We do our best to keep the app reliable, but we cannot guarantee that it always works or that nothing ever goes wrong. Don't use the app as your only source for legal or financial decisions.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may change these terms. For important changes we'll let you know in the app or by email. If you keep using the app, you agree to the new terms.

help.metaDescription: Forgot your password, can’t sign in or have a question about eezzyflow? Find your way here.
help.title: How can we help?
help.intro: Lost access to your account, can’t sign in or just have a question? Find your way here.
help.resetBody: Request a reset link. You’ll get an email to set a new password.
help.loginBody: Open the app and sign in with your email address and password.
help.formBody: Use the form in the app. You don’t need to be signed in.
help.mailBody: Prefer a regular email? Write to us and we’ll reply as soon as we can.
help.q1: I don’t receive the reset email
help.a1: Check your spam folder too, and make sure you use the address you signed up with. If nothing arrives after fifteen minutes, email us.
help.q2: I can’t get my two-step verification code anymore
help.a2: For example because you have a new phone. Sign in with your password and one of your ten recovery codes. Don’t have those either? Email us from your account’s email address.
help.q3: I can’t access my account’s mailbox anymore
help.a3: Email us with your name and the old email address. We’ll work out together how to confirm the account is yours.
help.q4: How do I delete my account?
help.a4: In the app, via Settings → Account → Delete account. Your data is then erased.
help.q5: How do I cancel my subscription?
help.legalBody: How we handle your data and what you can expect from us. Your data is stored in the European Union.

joinFaq.q: How does the other parent join?
joinFaq.a: You each have your own account, never a shared one. One parent creates an account, adds the children and invites the other parent via Family in the app. The other parent creates an account with the email address the invitation was sent to and accepts it. From then on you share the calendar, costs, messages and documents of those children. What is yours alone, such as your own address, stays private.

legal.websiteBody: eezzyflow.com uses no cookies, no trackers and no analytics. The website is hosted by Netlify; like any web host, Netlify briefly keeps technical data such as your IP address to serve the page. What follows is about the app.
